transcript: Our majority in the Senate is 51-49, but Senator McCain has been ill and hadn't been here since December. So we're 50-49. We can confirm people with a simple majority. But the Democrats in the Senate have been very obstructionist and preventing nominations from happening in a more routine fashion. So we end up spending a lot of time on personnel. For example, the week you were here, we did a circuit judge. We're going to confirm a secretary of state and confirm an ambassador to Germany. So we spent the whole week, this particular week, on the personnel portfolio, which is what's really different about the Senate. The House is not in the personnel business. There are over 1,200 executive branch appointments, subject to Senate confirmation. So we spend a lot of time, you know, helping the President get staffed up and also dealing with lifetime appointments to the courts, which has been a big priority of mine. As you may recall, I decided not to allow President Obama to fill the Scalia vacancy in the middle of the election on the Supreme Court. We've now filled that with a new judge, Justice Gorsuch, but we've also done 15 U.S. Circuit Court judges. That's the second step below the Supreme Court. Most litigation doesn't make it to the Supreme Court. Those are extremely important. We did 12 last year. That was more than the first year of any president since the Circuit Court system was created in 1891. So, yeah, we do a lot of person that will work around here in addition to legislation.
